A model at rest before a stimulus starts from a root of the right-hand side. `Pimpl()` computes
it numerically, `steadyStates()` in closed form. Guide:
[Setting up models](guide-model.html#steady-state-constraints).

## Conserved quantities

With compartment volumes $V_i$, stoichiometric coefficients $S_{ri}$ of species $i$ in reaction
$r$, and rates $v_r$ in a frame of volume $V_{f(r)}$, the right-hand side is

$$\dot x_i = f_i(x, p) = \frac{1}{V_i} \sum_r S_{ri}\, V_{f(r)}\, v_r(x, p). \tag{1}$$

Every $w$ with $S w = 0$ conserves the amount

$$\sum_i w_i V_i x_i \tag{2}$$

by (1); `conservedQuantities()` lists these amounts. Then $f(x, p) = 0$ does not determine $x$:
every conservation class, the states with given totals, has separate roots.

## Pseudo-transient continuation

For an `eqnlist`, `Pimpl()` adds the conservation laws $C(p)\, x = T$ of the stoichiometry, totals
$T$ as parameters:

$$G(x, p) = \begin{pmatrix} f(x, p) \\ C(p)\, x - T \end{pmatrix} = 0 . \tag{3}$$

Equations given as an `eqnvec` or character vector have no stoichiometry and are solved as they
are, so they have to determine $x$ themselves. With `flow = TRUE`, the default for an `eqnlist`,
pseudo-transient continuation solves (3) by implicit Euler steps of $\dot x = f(x, p)$ on the
conservation manifold, with a pseudo-time step that grows as the residual falls. It follows the flow
far from the root and becomes Newton's method near it. Newton steps may also reach an unstable
root, which the [stability test](#stability) catches. With `flow = FALSE`, the default otherwise,
the equations need not be the right-hand side of an ODE: the solver takes damped Newton steps,
without stability test, and returns any regular root. A state
no reaction changes keeps the given value. The solver is cppDE's `ptc()`, called from C++
([step, convergence and stability tests](https://dmodverse.github.io/cppDE/articles/methods-ptc.html)).

Every root starts from the same guess, a function of parameters and controls, never from an
earlier root, so the objective is the same function of the parameters in every call. Warm starts
would change roots in the last digits, which the ODE step-size control magnifies in the objective.

## Derivatives of the root

From $G(x(p), p) = 0$ for all $p$, the implicit function theorem gives

$$\frac{\partial G}{\partial x}\, \frac{\partial x}{\partial p} = -\frac{\partial G}{\partial p},
\tag{4}$$

regular where $J = \partial f / \partial x$ restricted to the conservation manifold,
$N^\top J N$ for a basis $N$ of $\ker C$, is nonsingular; such a root is isolated in the
conservation class. Where the matrix is singular, `Pimpl()` takes the pseudo-inverse and warns.
Differentiating (4) again gives the second derivatives, `Pimpl(deriv2 = TRUE)`, with the same
matrix. A reverse sweep applies the transpose of the solution $\partial x / \partial p$ of (4)
([Sensitivities and Hessians](methods-sensitivities.html#reverse-sweep)).

## Stability

A root is a resting state only if every eigenvalue $\lambda_k$ of $J = \partial f / \partial x$
on the conservation manifold has negative real part. At a root whose leading eigenvalue has real
part above `stabilityTol`, or above $10^{-8}$ of the largest eigenvalue modulus where that is
larger, the solver continues along the leading eigenvector
([cppDE](https://dmodverse.github.io/cppDE/articles/methods-ptc.html#stability)). Where neither
direction leads to a stable root, the next start is tried; the evaluation fails only when no start
reaches one. `controlsPTC = list(stability = FALSE)` returns
the unstable root.

`constraintStability()` adds a term that rises towards the stability boundary:

$$\kappa \sum_k r_k^2, \qquad
  r_k = \frac{\max\bigl(0,\ \mathrm{Re}\,\lambda_k - \lambda_0\bigr)}{\lambda_{tol} - \lambda_0},
  \tag{5}$$

with weight $\kappa$, $\lambda_{tol}$ the `stabilityTol` of the `Pimpl()` and the onset
$\lambda_0$ given as `onset`, or $\lambda_0 = \lambda_{tol} - 1/t_D$ from `duration` $= t_D$, the
time the data span. The term is zero while every perturbation decays faster than the
experiment lasts. Steady states that agree in all inputs count once. For a simple eigenvalue with
right and left eigenvectors $u_k$, $v_k$ of $J$, $v_k^{\mathsf H} u_k \ne 0$, and (4),

$$
  \frac{\mathrm{d}\lambda_k}{\mathrm{d}p}
  = \frac{v_k^{\mathsf H} \bigl(\partial_p J + \partial_x J\, \mathrm{d}x^*/\mathrm{d}p\bigr) u_k}
         {v_k^{\mathsf H} u_k},
  \tag{6}
$$

which needs `Pimpl(deriv2 = TRUE)`. The term is a model assumption, not data: profiles with
`stop = "data"` and likelihood ratios leave it out.

At the onset, (5) and the gradient are continuous and the curvature jumps: below, term and Hessian
are zero; above, the Gauss-Newton Hessian is

$$\frac{2 \kappa}{(\lambda_{tol} - \lambda_0)^2} \sum_{k \,:\, \mathrm{Re}\,\lambda_k > \lambda_0}
  \frac{\mathrm{d}\,\mathrm{Re}\,\lambda_k}{\mathrm{d}p}
  \frac{\mathrm{d}\,\mathrm{Re}\,\lambda_k}{\mathrm{d}p}^{\mathsf T} , \tag{7}$$

nonzero as $\mathrm{Re}\,\lambda_k \to \lambda_0$. A profile therefore takes small steps across
the onset ([Profile likelihood](methods-profiles.html#computing-a-profile)).

## Analytical steady-state constraints

`steadyStates()` solves $f(x, p) = 0$ in closed form [@rosenblatt2016customized; @kaschek2019dmod].
Each unknown, a state or a kinetic parameter, is solved from a combination of balances such that
the solution is a ratio of sums of positive terms. The solution is thus positive for positive
parameters, also with `solveQuadratic = TRUE`, which takes the positive root of a balance quadratic
in the state. A state whose balance is spent on a kinetic parameter stays free, as the parameter of the
steady-state value of the state. States that are zero in every steady state are set to 0. A conserved quantity
keeps one state free. Volumes are never solved for.

The result, one equation per solved unknown, replaces identity entries of a parameter
transformation:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
steady <- steadyStates(reactions)
parameters <- getParameters(reactions)
trafo <- repar(eqnvec(setNames(parameters, parameters)), "x <- y",
               x = names(steady), y = steady)
p <- P(trafo)
```

| argument | effect |
|---|---|
| `givenCQs` | conserved quantities, default from `customTotals()` or derived |
| `neglect` | states and parameters never solved for |
| `priority` | states solved first, parameters preferred as pivots |
| `forcings` | states held at zero as exogenous inputs |
| `solveQuadratic` | allow the positive root of a quadratic balance |
| `file` | save the result with `saveRDS()` |

Without a solution of this form, `steadyStates()` returns `0`. The solver is a Python module
(numpy, sympy, scipy) called through reticulate.

`P()` or `Pexpl()` evaluate the closed form explicitly with symbolic derivatives: no root search, no
convergence failure, no solver tolerance in the objective, one parameter less per solved equation.
Rosenblatt et al. report more reliable and faster optimization than with common numerical
implementations [@rosenblatt2016customized]. `steadyStates()` does not test stability; `Pimpl()`
does ([Stability](#stability)). `Pimpl()` is needed where no closed form of positive sums exists,
as for the network of the guide.

Reference: `conservedQuantities()`, `Pimpl()`, `steadyStates()`, `constraintStability()`
